Screen Time, Study, and University Workload

Akasha Shroff

Introduction

This visual data story explores observational logging data related to screen time, university workload, phone use, sleep, and study habits. The data was collected through a Google Form completed daily. The purpose of this analysis is to investigate patterns between workload, productivity, and personal habits.

Screen time patterns

Bar chart showing the number of observations in each screen time category.

This graph shows how frequently different screen time categories occurred across the logged observations.

Phone pickups and screen time

Column chart showing average phone pickups across screen time categories.

This graph compares average phone pickups between different screen time categories. Higher screen time categories generally appear alongside more frequent phone pickups.

Sleep and study hours

Column chart showing average study hours for each sleep range.

This graph explores whether sleep duration may be related to the amount of personal study completed.

Assignments over time

Line graph showing total assignments due across dates.

This graph uses timestamp data converted with lubridate to show how assignment workload changed over time.

Conclusion

Overall, the visualisations suggest relationships between screen time, phone usage, sleep, and academic workload. Observational logging provides useful insight into daily study behaviours and productivity patterns.
